preconditions.description: n is the number of people (1 ≤ n ≤ 100,000) and k is the number of imbalanced people (0 ≤ k ≤ n).

postconditions.description: If no valid construction exists, output 'NO'. Otherwise, output 'YES' followed by exactly n integers (s_1, ..., s_n) representing the child of each person (0 ≤ s_i ≤ n).

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(s_i) <= n for s_i in stdout.split()[1:]) if stdout.split()[0] == 'YES' else True
postconditions.description: Each s_i in the output must be an integer between 0 and n (inclusive), where 0 indicates no child.

postconditions.expression: any(s_i == 0 for s_i in stdout.split()[1:]) if stdout.split()[0] == 'YES' else True
postconditions.description: Exactly one person has no child (s_i = 0).

postconditions.expression: all(s_i != i for i, s_i in enumerate(stdout.split()[1:], 1)) if stdout.split()[0] == 'YES' else True
postconditions.description: No person is their own child (s_i ≠ i for all i).

postconditions.expression: all((s_i == 0 and all(s_j != i for j in range(1, n + 1))) or (s_i != 0 and all(s_j != s_i for j in range(1, n + 1))) for i, s_i in enumerate(stdout.split()[1:], 1)) if stdout.split()[0] == 'YES' else True
postconditions.description: Each person has either both parents or none (no cycles or self-references in parent-child relationships).

postconditions.expression: sum(1 for i in range(1, n + 1) if is_imbalanced(i, stdout.split()[1:])) == k if stdout.split()[0] == 'YES' else True
postconditions.description: The total number of imbalanced people in the constructed structure equals k.
